title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-30
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 6NT. West's opening spade lead is overtaken by East. South has only 11 top tricks. East should be allowed to win at trick 1 in an attempt to rectify the count for a squeeze. East shifts to a heart won in dummy.

A low club should be played from North. When East discards, his most likely shape is 7330 (West rates to be longer than East in both hearts and diamonds). If that is the case, the defense will be subject to a compound squeeze.

South should cash all of the clubs in the closed hand, overtaking the last round with North's ♣A. East must keep his spades and must, therefore, give up his guard in either hearts or diamonds.

If East discards a heart West will have the only heart guard. A double squeeze will operate with diamonds being the suit guarded by both East and West. South crosses in diamonds and cashes the ♠A. A heart is played to the dummy and the last club will squeeze both defenders, East in spades and diamonds and West in hearts and diamonds.

If East discards a diamond on the second last club a similar fate awaits the defense. Again there will be a double squeeze, but this time hearts will be the suit guarded by both defenders.

The last club is cashed immediately and South discards the ♦2. South crosses in diamonds. West will be squeezed in diamonds and hearts on the play of the ♠A. East will be squeezed in spades and hearts when the other top diamond is cashed.
